strengths: Novel asymmetric cross-modal interaction mechanism that thoughtfully balances convergence speed and performance through modality-specific aligners (A2V and V2A with different temporal strategies)
Significant practical efficiency improvements: achieves strong results with 1.3M training samples vs. 30.7M for Ovi and 6.4M for UniVerse-1, demonstrating efficient cross-modal learning
Comprehensive multi-dimensional evaluation including audio quality (PQ, CU, WER), video quality (SC, DD, IQ), and audio-video consistency (LS, TC, EC) metrics
Thorough ablation studies validating each component (ACMI design, FAM effectiveness, MA-CFG impact, training strategies) with clear performance improvements
Strong generalization to out-of-distribution data: anime image example (Fig. 4b) shows clear advantages over Ovi and UniVerse-1 where competitors fail
Elegant unified framework supporting multiple audio-video tasks (joint generation, continuation, video-to-audio dubbing, audio-driven synthesis) without task-specific model designs
Clear presentation with effective visualizations, particularly Fig. 3 comparing interaction mechanisms and Fig. 4 showing qualitative results
Well-motivated technical contributions with clear articulation of limitations in prior work (global vs. symmetric temporal-aligned approaches)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty in individual components: dual-branch architecture directly adopts existing models (Wan 2.2-5B, 2.1-1.3B), cross-attention is standard, and mask prediction is straightforward. Novelty is primarily in combination and asymmetric interaction design

Small evaluation set (100 test samples, only 50 real-world) is insufficient for robust claims about generalization and competitive advantage; single OOD anime example inadequate for demonstrating OOD robustness
No user studies despite focus on synchronization and emotional consistency where human perception is critical; results rely entirely on automated metrics
LLM-based evaluation (Gemini-2.5-Pro) for timbre/emotion consistency is unvalidated with no inter-rater reliability reported; LLMs may have systematic biases and this approach lacks peer consensus

Reproducibility concerns: internally collected training dataset for Stage 2/3 not characterized (size, quality, accessibility); no code/model release plans mentioned; cannot fully verify experimental setup
Missing critical technical details: window size w for A2V context not specified, λm decay schedule undefined, task ratio selection (4:1:1:2:2) unjustified with no ablation study

Fairness of baseline comparisons: two-stage methods use different audio generation (F5-TTS), JavisDiT not designed for human speech, and UniVerse-1 performance anomalously poor (nearly static), suggesting possible implementation issues
Face-aware modulation assumes facial regions always dominate audio-video coupling; limited to human-centric scenarios with unclear generalization to other content types

No failure case analysis, no evaluation of content type performance variation, no computational cost comparisons, and missing sensitivity analyses (window size w, interpolation granularity, mask threshold effects)
Marginal improvements on some metrics: lip-sync (5.95 vs 6.48 for Ovi is worse), and some ablation improvements are small (Table 3: unsupervised FAM shows minimal difference from supervised)
